text:
Christopher Columbus

Frederick stared at the glowing runes, the weight of eternity pressing against his mortal heart. The draft intensified, swirling the pages of the ancient book into a frenzy. He reached for the vial of iridescent liquid, his fingers trembling not from fear, but from the sheer magnitude of the choice. To drink was to step outside the river of time, to watch civilizations rise and fall while he remained unchanged. To destroy it was to accept the finality of death, to let the secret return to the void from which it came.

Instead of reaching for the vial or the book, Frederick pulled a small, iron-bound box from his coat. He had spent years preparing for this moment, not to use the potion, but to ensure it could never be misused. With a steady hand, he placed the book inside the box and sealed it with a wax sigil that would melt only in the heart of a volcano. He then poured the potion ingredients into a small clay pot, mixed them with ash from the altar, and cast the mixture into the brazier. The flames turned a deep, sorrowful blue before dying out completely.

Frederick took a deep breath, the air suddenly feeling lighter. He had chosen mortality, not out of cowardice, but out of respect for the natural order. He closed the iron box, locked it, and walked out of the hidden chamber, leaving the secret of eternal life to remain just that—a secret. As he emerged into the sunlight, he felt the warmth on his skin, a fleeting, precious sensation that he now knew was all the more valuable because it would one day end.
